ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Joe Louis

code.originalText: Ten-week review: remission, the antipsychotic taper, cognition off cocaine, the echocardiogram and a one-day return to use

text.paragraph: Ten-week review: remission, antipsychotic taper, cognition and the echocardiogram. [S]

Mr. Louis returns one week after his preventive visit. He has had no persecutory beliefs for about six weeks and sleeps six to seven hours. In the last week of August he was out of town for four days of paid appearances and missed two urine tests; the day after he came home, with an old acquaintance, he used cocaine on one day. He reported it himself at his next test, which was positive, and all tests since have been negative. He had no psychotic symptoms after that use. His stool test kit came back negative. His home readings average 128/80 mmHg. The echocardiogram was done this morning. [S]

list.item:
Cocaine use disorder, severe, with cocaine-induced psychotic disorder, psychosis in remission (F14.250). Six weeks without psychotic symptoms. The ASAM/AAAP guideline advises a gradual taper off the antipsychotic after a period of remission when the psychosis was stimulant-induced, and he would like to stop. One day of cocaine use after a trip, reported by him; a return to use is common in recovery and is met without blame. MoCA 27 after ten weeks with good sleep and no psychotic symptoms, up from 25 during symptoms; with a normal MRI, there is no evidence of a neurocognitive disorder, and no research label such as traumatic encephalopathy syndrome is applied. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone. [S]
Aripiprazole 2 mg each morning for two weeks, then stop; call at once if the fears or sleeplessness return.
Continue contingency management to the end of twelve weeks and weekly therapy.
Travel plan: urine tests at a partner clinic and phone therapy sessions when away.
MoCA yearly.

Hypertension on amlodipine (I10). Echocardiogram: ejection fraction 60%, mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, normal valves, aortic root 3.6 cm and ascending aorta 3.5 cm, both normal. Clinic 130/82 and home average 128/80 mmHg: near target. [S]
Continue amlodipine 5 mg.
He was told that cocaine raises the risk of heart attack, stroke and tearing of the aorta, and to call 911 for chest or back pain.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2023); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia (2020); Treatment for Stimulant Use Disorders (Treatment Improvement Protocol 33, updated 2021) (2021); National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Traumatic Encephalopathy Syndrome (2021); 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Fifteen-week review in five weeks, after the taper. Contingency management to the end of twelve weeks; therapy weekly. Call the clinic or 988 if the fears or sleeplessness return. Next scheduled visit 2026-10-26: fifteen-week review off the antipsychotic: recovery, blood pressure and finances. [S]
